lawyer:
Md. Shahjahan with SM Amin Azhar, Advocates ----- For the Appellants.

Nehal Uddin (Md) and others ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Amena Khatunand others ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
"Since after purchase of the s/1 plaintiff possessed the s/1 through adhiars, Jamsher, Jamattulla, Dasimuddin and Mafizuddin for 10/11 years. Thereafter she had the s/1 in direct khas possession for 5/6 yrs. For the last 7/8 yrs. the s/1 is again being possessed through adhiars Kasimuddin and Safaruddin among some other persons. Defendant Nos. 2-4 have also been adhiars with respect to the s/1 for 7/8 yrs. The land sold away to defendants 12/15 are being possessed by the vendor themselves. Defendant Nos. 5 and 6 never possessed the s/1 or any portion of the suit joie after execution of Ext. 1 "In cross-examination this witness stated that defendants 2-4 are co-sharers in the suit property. In CS khatian defendants 5 and 6 were co-sharers, the CS Khatian bears also the names of these two defendants." 

 19. PW 2 Dasimuddin Akand states that they adhi cultivated 3-3½ bighas of land under Amena Khatun for 10/11 yrs. Thereafter for 4/5 years she got the same cultivated by her servants. Solaiman among others has been cultivating the s/1 at present. In cross-examination this witness stated that the adhiars were not known to the husband of the plaintiff and Solaiman was never an adhiar with respect to the s/1. He gave the description of the boundaries of the suit land. He stated that he himself gave adhi crops to the plaintiff. PW 3 stated that defendants 2-4 had been cultivating as adhiars under Mvi. A Rahman, PW 1 for 5/7 years, previously Abdur Rahman Mia kept the suit land in khas possession for 3/4 years. Defendants 5 and 6 were 5-7 years old and they never possessed the suit land. In cross examination this witness stated that he was not adhiar under PW.1 at that time. He stated that defendants 2-4 had been cultivating the suit land as adhiars since after his surrender in 1390 BS. He stated that defendants 2-4 are nephews of defendants No. 5-6. PW 4 Najamuddin drummer stated that he had been cultivating as adhiar under PW 1 for 5/6 years. He stated that he did not know whether Rabeya and Jamila ever possessed the suit land. In cross-examination this witness stated that he did not remember in which year he had taken adhi. He also stated that he did not know the area of the land. He admitted that defendants 2-4 also possessed the suit land. PW 5 Sarafuddin stated that he was cultivating 12/14 kathas of the suit land under Abdur Rahman Mia, for 5/7 years and also stated that Rabeya and Jamila never possessed the suit land. In cross examination this witnesses stated that defendants 2-4 purchased some land from his share in the suit property and by virtue of that purchase. Nehaluddin and others had been possessing a portion of the suit land. He could not tell the month and the year in which he had taken adhi. PW 6 Abdul Gafur Munshi stated that he himself sold the entire share of his father to defendant Nos. 2-4 and that Rabeya and Jamila never possessed the suit land. He stated that he was adhiar under PW 1 in respect of some other lands. He admitted that women did not cultivate the land themselves and they cultivated by their brothers and husbands and that the homestead of defendants 2-4 stood on the suit property. DW 7 Ismail Uddin Akhand stated that nobody on behalf of the defendants 5 and 7 possessed the suit land. In cross examination he stated that he could not say which plots were cultivated by whom. DW 8 Yunus Ali stated that he was no attesting witness to Ext. 1. He had no land in the suit mouza. DW 9 Nasu Sk. stated that he filed Ext. lc-Id. He stated that defendant Nos. 2-4 possessed the suit lands other than the Kabala lands. 

 22. Now, from the consideration and analysis of the above evidence, it appears that the plaintiff claimed possession over the disputed portion of the suit jote in three different ways, firstly, for 10/11 years through some bargadars and again through khas possession for 4/5 years and then again through the present defendants 2-4 but these defendants stated that they were bargadars under defendant Nos. 5 and 6 and used to give crops to the said defendant Nos. 5 and 6 and after their own purchase, they have been possessing suit property independently as their own. It is the case of the plaintiff that she was in ejmali possession of the suit property and admittedly there has been no partition of the suit property by metes and bounds. Furthermore, from the deposition of the DW 4, it appear that the suit property was recorded in the present khatians in the names of the Air Tran defendants including the names of defendant Nos. 5 and 6. It is of course true that the record of right cannot be a document of title but it may be used as documentary evidence to show possession. Now, title by way of adverse possession has been claimed by the plaintiff and as such the onus is upon the plaintiff to establish the conditions required for acquisition of title by adverse possession. In view of the decisions cited above, it is no doubt clear that in the case of a claim of title by adverse possession by a co-sharer against another co-sharer, ouster of the latter has to be proved and possession of the party claiming title by adverse possession must be actual and exclusive for a continuous period of more than 12 years in assertion of hostile title. From the evidence on record as discussed above, it does not appear that the plaintiff has been able to fulfill the above conditions by reliable and sufficient evidence. It is rather the case of the plaintiff that she possessed the suit property in ejmali with other co-sharers through bargadars, but she could not lead any evidence to prove ouster of the other co-sharers particularly defendant Nos. 5 and 6 from their portion of the suit lands.
